context: area network · pre-insulated chilled-water pipe, welded and tested; ETS in each building; flushing governs the end

brief.intro: New to this project type? A district cooling network carries chilled water from a central plant to many buildings and brings the warmed water back, through a pair of large buried pipes (supply and return). The pipe is steel, factory pre-insulated inside a plastic jacket with a leak-detection wire in the foam. On site the lengths are welded, each weld is tested, and the joint is then insulated and sealed. In the basement of each building an energy transfer station (ETS) — heat exchangers, valves and a meter — connects the network to the building's own system. Because the pipes are large and come in pairs, the trench is wide and takes a big share of the utility corridor. The end of the job is dominated by flushing and cleaning the pipes to the plant's water-quality standard.

glossary.plain: the pipe carrying chilled water out to the buildings and the pipe bringing warmer water back.
steel pipe supplied with foam insulation and an outer plastic jacket already on it.
the sleeve fitted over a welded joint and filled with foam to complete the insulation.
wires in the foam that raise an alarm, and locate the spot, if water gets into the insulation.
the heat-exchanger set in a building that connects it to the network without mixing the water.
the temperature difference between return and supply water; the network is sized for it.
circulating water fast enough to carry out debris; repeated until the water is clean.

the unit of cooling capacity — tons of refrigeration.

must_get_right: Reserve the corridor early: two large pipes need a wide trench, and they compete with every other utility in the road.
Welding output per qualified welder sets the pace; each weld needs testing and each joint needs foaming and an alarm-wire check before backfill.
Flushing and chemical cleaning are long (weeks), need large temporary pumps and water, and must be accepted by the plant operator — give them their own section of the schedule.
Each building's ETS room must be ready, and each customer's own system must be ready, before chilled water can be supplied; track both building by building.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by network section between valve chambers and by building (ETS), so each customer connection can be read from trench to chilled-water-on.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar; welding and joint foaming are sensitive to rain and to very high temperatures. Flushing runs continuously once started.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Per section: trench → lay → weld → NDT → joint casing and foam → alarm-wire test → hydrotest → backfill. Network: all sections → flushing → chemical cleaning → water quality accepted → fill → connection to the plant → balancing. Each building: ETS room ready → ETS installed → customer side ready → chilled water on.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The corridor is reserved and free; the cooling plant is ready to receive the network on the assumed date; ETS rooms are handed over by the building contractors; flushing water and discharge are available.

sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

rows: Before pipe laying in each section

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: The wide trench limits traffic and other utilities; the pipe must be kept dry and capped at all times; welders must be qualified to the procedure.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: corridor clashes, water entering the insulation, weld repairs, late ETS rooms, and repeated flushing cycles to reach water quality. Contingency is held before the chilled-water-on date of the first customer.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by network section and building; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the trench, welding and jointing teams — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
